{{Short description|FIFA World Cup group}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2025}}
{{Use American English|date=November 2025}}
Group K of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] took place from June 17 to 27, 2026.<ref name="match schedule">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 26 – Match Schedule |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=February 4, 2024}}</ref> The group consisted of [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]], [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo]], [[Uzbekistan national football team|Uzbekistan]], and [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]].

Colombia secured their advancement to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 Regulations |publisher=FIFA |date=May 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623212158/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> after two group game wins, and would top the group after earning a draw against Portugal. Portugal also advanced as group runners-up, after a crucial victory against Uzbekistan.

Although DR Congo failed to win their first two matches, a victory over Uzbekistan allowed them to finish third in the group and advance as one of the best third-place teams.<ref name="regulations">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 Regulations |publisher=FIFA |date=May 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623212158/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> Uzbekistan finished fourth and were eliminated, losing all three of their group games.

==Standings==
{{2026 FIFA World Cup group tables|Group K}}

In the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]]:<ref name="regulations"/>
* The winner of Group K, [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]], advanced to play the third-place team of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group L|Group L]], [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]].
* The runner-up of Group K, [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]], advanced to play the runner-up of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group L|Group L]], [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]].
* The third-place team of Group K, [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo]], advanced to play the winner of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group L|Group L]], [[England national football team|England]], as one of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|eight best third-place teams]] from the group stage.

==Matches==
All times listed are local.<ref name="match schedule"/>

===Portugal vs DR Congo===
The two teams had never met before.

This match marked the country's first time competing under the name DR Congo, having previously appeared as ''Zaire'' in [[1974 FIFA World Cup|1974]]. It was also the first World Cup match to be played within the vicinity of a tropical cyclone ([[Tropical Storm Arthur (2026)|Tropical Storm Arthur]]), but it was unaffected.

Portugal captain [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] matched Argentina's [[Lionel Messi]] by playing in a sixth World Cup finals, and also become the oldest outfield player to start a World Cup match at the age of 41 years and 132 days.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cjrg2r5pyl8t?page=3|title= Portugal 1 DR Congo 1|date=17 June 2026|work=BBC Sport |accessdate=18 June 2026}}</ref>

Portugal went in front in the 6th minute when [[João Neves]] headed to the right corner after a cross from the left by [[Pedro Neto]]. In time added on in the first half, it was 1–1 when [[Yoane Wissa]] headed to the left of the net from six yards out after a cross from the right by [[Arthur Masuaku]], the goal was DR Congo's first-ever World Cup final's goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/17/portugal-dr-congo-world-cup-2026-group-k-match-report|title= Yoane Wissa gives DR Congo first ever World Cup point in draw with Portugal|date=17 June 2026|work=Guardian |accessdate=18 June 2026}}</ref>

===Uzbekistan vs Colombia===
The two teams had never met before. It was the first time since May 12, 2002 that Colombia returned to the pitch of the Azteca having lost a friendly match there to [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] 2–1. The fixture marked Uzbekistan's debut at the FIFA World Cup.

In the 40th minute, [[Daniel Muñoz (footballer)|Daniel Muñoz]] put Colombia in front when he scored with a volley from six yards out, connecting with a pass over the top from [[Luis Díaz (footballer, born 1997)|Luis Díaz]]. [[Abbosbek Fayzullaev]] made it 1–1 in the 60th minute when he headed into an empty net from close range after Colombian goalkeeper had parried a shot from [[Eldor Shomurodov]] on the right. The goal was Uzbekistan's first-ever goal at a World Cup finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/world-cup-2026/2026/0617/1578917-classy-colombia-have-too-much-for-debutants-uzbekistan/|title= Classy Colombia have too much for debutants Uzbekistan|date=17 June 2026|work=RTE Sport |accessdate=18 June 2026}}</ref>
Colombia went back in front five minutes later when Luis Díaz scored with a low finish to the right corner. In the 9th minute of added time, substitute [[Jaminton Campaz]] made it 3–1 when he headed to the left corner of the net from six yards out after a cross from [[Cucho Hernández]] on the right.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ced4nx35648t|title= Uzbekistan 1 Colombia 3|date=17 June 2026|work=BBC Sport |accessdate=18 June 2026}}</ref>

[[Abdukodir Khusanov]] received a yellow card for a tackle on [[Luis Díaz (footballer, born 1997)|Luis Díaz]] that caused him to collide with a pitch-side camera operator. The match was briefly paused while medical staff attended to the cameraman, who was taken to the hospital but escaped serious injury. Following the match, Khusanov sent a signed match jersey with a written apology to the operator.<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 June 2026 |title=Ukbekistan's Khusanov sends apology shirt to cameraman injured in World Cup opener |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/ukbekistans-khusanov-sends-apology-shirt-cameraman-injured-world-cup-opener-2026-06-18/ |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

===Portugal vs Uzbekistan===
The two teams had never met before.

[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] scored twice in the first half, becoming the first player to score in six FIFA World Cup tournaments.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/portugal-vs-uzbekistan-live-updates-world-cup-2026-score-result/BgWNd0QLnPcl/JjwI4QH7ycFz/ |title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores at record sixth World Cup as Portugal thrash Uzbekistan: Live updates and reaction |publisher=The New York Times |date=23 June 2026 }}</ref>

This fixture was the second-largest defeat suffered by an Asian team during the tournament's group stage, following Qatar's [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group B#Canada vs Qatar|6–0 loss]] to [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]] and tied with Iraq's [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group I#Senegal vs Iraq|5–0 loss]] against [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] 3 days later.

===Colombia vs DR Congo===
The two teams had never met before.

In the 76th minute, [[Daniel Muñoz (footballer)|Daniel Muñoz]] scored the only goal of the game with a low finish from the right that was deflected and went in at the near post.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/clywx7rkx9kt|title= Colombia 1 DR Congo 0|date=23 June 2026|work=BBC Sport |accessdate=24 June 2026}}</ref>

===Colombia vs Portugal===
The two teams had never met before.

Both teams struggled to make goals from either side, with [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] missing his shots throughout. In the end, both teams finished with a 0–0 draw, with [[Diogo Costa]] earning Man of the Match for his consistent performance.

===DR Congo vs Uzbekistan===
[[File:2026 FIFA World Cup Match 72, DR Congo v Uzbekistan.webp|thumb|Pre-match anthems between DR Congo and Uzbekistan]]

The two teams had never met before.

Uzbekistan scored an early lead against the determined DR Congo team by [[Eldor Shomurodov]] in the first half, though a costly mistake in the second half resulted in [[Yoane Wissa]] to score an equalizer. Additional goals by [[Fiston Mayele]] and Yoane Wissa secured DR Congo's spot in the knockout phase for the first time ever.

For Uzbekistan, three straight defeats meant they were eliminated from the group stage alongside fellow debutant [[Jordan national football team|Jordan]], who also went winless with three straight defeats [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group J#Jordan vs Argentina|in their group]].

==Discipline==
The team conduct ("fair play") score would have been used as a tiebreaker if the head-to-head and overall records of teams were tied. It would also be used as a tiebreaker for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|third-place ranking]] between groups if the overall records of teams were tied. The score was calculated based on yellow and red cards received by players and team officials in all group matches as follows:<ref name="regulations"/>
*yellow card: −1 point;
*indirect red card (second yellow card): −3 points;
*direct red card: −4 points;
*yellow card and direct red card: −5 points;

Only one of the above deductions could be applied to a player or team official in a single match.
